source.title: Implicit Bias in Noisy-SGD: With Applications to Differentially Private Training
source.authors: Tom Sander; Maxime Sylvestre; A. Durmus

record.file_problem: none; full paper text including supplementary material is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether batch size affects held-out performance using Noisy-SGD, a different method from the large-batch comparisons named in V5.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports the study's ImageNet batch-size comparison. The DP-SGD crosses are from Sander et al. (2023), so they are not extracted as this study's results. The DLN experiments concern sparse regression and do not test natural-label generalization or the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The ImageNet experiment compares batch sizes at fixed gradient steps, whereas V5 specifies fixed epochs. Larger batches therefore receive more training examples and epochs. This result does not establish the batch-size effect under V5's budget condition. The remaining experiments test implicit bias in sparse regression, outside the listed versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report declining ImageNet performance with increasing batch size under fixed-step Noisy-SGD training and interpret this as evidence that SGD's noise geometry remains influential despite Gaussian perturbations. Their DLN analysis and experiments further show that appropriately vanishing additional noise can enhance implicit bias toward sparse solutions.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Noisy-SGD without clipping and adds isotropic Gaussian noise; the ImageNet comparison fixes steps and effective noise σ/B. The DLN analysis uses a continuous model with decreasing noise.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes test accuracy in the ImageNet experiment; the text reports that small batches perform better than larger ones at fixed steps and σ/B.

fits_no_version.finding: Smaller batches yield better ImageNet test accuracy with Noisy-SGD at fixed 72k gradient steps and fixed effective Gaussian noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large batches can reduce image-classification accuracy under fixed update budgets even when isotropic Gaussian noise is added without gradient clipping.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic sparse regression, DLNs trained with the studied vanishing-noise update recover solutions closer to the sparse ground truth than standard SGD, across the tested initializations and noise levels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Additional Gaussian noise can improve SGD's implicit bias toward sparse solutions in diagonal linear networks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS) 2024
record.problems: The ImageNet result is presented as a figure without exact values in the text. The comparison fixes gradient steps rather than epochs, and Noisy-SGD is a proxy for DP-SGD; the authors note that it only aligns with DP-SGD under bounded-gradient assumptions.
record.rows_left_out: The DP-SGD crosses in Figure 1 are attributed to Sander et al. (2023), not this study. DLN sparse-regression results in Figures 3–7 and Sections 3.3, 4.2, and Appendix B concern sparsity and solution distance, not the claim versions' natural-label test-error outcomes.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and whether adapted training recipes remove the penalty.
Effects of dropout and its interaction with training-set size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor of generalization gaps.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The fixed-step design is an untested condition of V5, not evidence warranting limits_scope. Figure 1's DP-SGD crosses are attributed to Sander et al. (2023) and are correctly excluded as this study's results. The DLN results are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

The experiment fixes gradient steps, not epochs; it does not test longer training, learning-rate scaling with warmup, normalization or regularization changes, or the other cited studies' image and language settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison with other generalization measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples.

rows.subject: Normalizer-Free ResNets (NF-ResNets)
rows.operation_detail: Train with Noisy-SGD while varying batch size at a fixed number of steps and fixed effective noise σ/B.

conditions.value: different batch sizes; exact values figure only

rows.note: The text says small batches perform better than larger ones. The plotted values are not stated in the text; the comparison holds steps and σ/B fixed.
rows.check: The caption explicitly reports worse test accuracy for larger batches, but the fixed-72k-step comparison cannot determine V5's fixed-epoch effect. The qualitative finding is valid; exact batch sizes and accuracies are unavailable in the supplied figure text. Add the weight exponential moving average with decay 0.999 to the recipe.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
